issues.description: The Bitmap24 class in the template header declares its constructors, public API methods, and data members under the private section, while example_program/main.cpp (and other code) instantiates and uses Bitmap24 (constructors, resize_buffer, set, save) as if they were public. The solution's Bitmap24.hpp exposes these members as public. The template's private visibility for the constructor and methods prevents students from compiling/running the example and is a structural mismatch between template and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template's example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp, move the constructors, destructor, and public API (resize_buffer, save, set) and the width/height/data members into the public section (or declare the needed constructors and methods public). This will align the template with the usage in main.cpp and with the solution header, allowing the example to compile and avoiding student confusion.
